turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in and sit down there. You look worn out, if you don't mind me saying. How have you been keeping?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm fine. I'm grand. It was the wife who booked this, not me.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. What had her worried, would you say?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The sleep, mostly. She says I'm up half the night and I've no energy the next day. I told her I'm fine.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you fine, though, or is that the short answer to make it go away?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Well. I'm tired — knackered, actually — and I can't get interested in anything, the telly or the garden or the lads. Months of it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Months is a while. Can you put any kind of date on when it started?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I haven't a clue, honestly. Last winter, or the one before, around when I was let go from the depot. Could've been after Christmas, could've been before — I can't give you a date.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's all right, we don't need the exact day. The job — a redundancy, was it?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Twenty-two years in the one place and a letter. I'm still rattling round the house like a spare part.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): That'd take the stuffing out of anyone. With the sleep, is it getting off, or waking early, or the both?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): The both. I lie there till two — well, actually nearer three some nights — with the mind going ninety, and then I'm awake again around five. Not every night. Most nights.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): And through the day, the energy?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Flat. I could be on the couch from eleven and still feel useless. Half the time I don't even switch the telly on.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): The loss of interest — is the mood low along with it, or more just numb?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Low in myself. Snappy with the wife, which isn't fair, and I don't ring anyone. Dinner doesn't taste of anything — I'm not even hungry in a... no, the eating's the same, I'm just not enjoying it.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the appetite itself hasn't changed, and no weight loss that you've noticed?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Eating the same. Weight's the same. She's still cooking for four.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): I have to ask you something straight, the way I ask everyone in this spot. Any thoughts of hurting yourself, or of not wanting to be here at all?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that — I'm miserable, not stupid, and I wouldn't lay a hand on myself. The two kids are still in the house, for God's sake.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you can say it plain. Anything else in the body — chest pain, shortness of breath?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain, breathing's grand. It's the head and the get-up-and-go, that's the whole of it. The spaniel's been walking herself, a dog with more of a routine than me.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): She'll cope. Are you taking any medicines just now?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the blood pressure one. Ramipril. That's it.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nurse read it off the sheet for me just now — ramipril five milligrams, once every morning.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): That's wrong. It's ten. Ten milligrams, and it's been ten a long while. She has the old number, so don't write five.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll leave the strength blank till we check it against the repeat script. Nothing else — no sleeping tablet, nothing over the counter?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't take anything else. I nearly said the wife has something for her own sleep, but that's hers, not mine. I never took it.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine, or to anything else?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. Never had a reaction that I know of.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke? And what about drink?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked in my life. A few pints of a weekend, same as always. Maybe the one extra since the job went. Not every night, before you ask.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): How are the days filled, if you're not in work?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Signing on. The odd walk when the dog makes a show of me. Otherwise the kitchen and the racing on the radio. Fierce boring.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're looking tired even while we're talking, and the speech is a bit flat. No restlessness, though, and no shake in the hands.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, well, I didn't sleep, so. Sorry if I'm sharp. The waiting room was roasting and yer man on the phone wouldn't give it a rest.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): No apology. From what you've told me, this has the shape of a low mood after the redundancy — the sleep, the interest gone, the energy gone. I wouldn't put a firm diagnosis on it today.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): So I'm not losing it, then. Grand.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're not losing it. We could think about a small dose of sertraline later if this hasn't lifted, but I'm not starting any medicine today. I'd rather see what a few ordinary weeks do.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I'd rather no tablet. Not yet. Tablets for the head... I don't know. Maybe if I'm still like this.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's a fair way to leave it. Try to get out of the house once a day, even twenty minutes, and keep the bed for sleep instead of lying awake stewing. If a thought of harming yourself ever does show up, ring the surgery that same day or go to the emergency department — don't wait it out.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. I hear you. I'll tell the wife, she'll be on my case anyway.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in four weeks, better or not, and we'll decide about a tablet then.

spec.situation: Adult with poor sleep, low energy and loss of interest for months after a job loss or bereavement; partner or parent speaks for them; patient says 'I'm fine' then partly opens up; denies thoughts of self-harm clearly (doctor asks gently); medication discussed but not started today.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

omissions.text: Current ramipril dose is stated by the patient to be 10 mg once every morning; the listed 5 mg on the nurse sheet is wrong.
Insomnia details not captured: both difficulty falling asleep and early waking, lying awake until about 2-3 am and waking again around 5 am, most nights.
Social withdrawal/isolation: patient does not ring anyone.
Anhedonia detail: no longer interested in usual activities including the TV, gardening, and seeing 'the lads'; often does not even switch the TV on.
Patient reports feeling miserable and 'not stupid' and says he would not lay a hand on himself because his two kids are still in the house; this strengthens the denial of self-harm/suicidal intent.
Patient prefers not to start medication yet and specifically says he would rather no tablet for his mood at this stage.
